signDesignCopy.introduction: A sign is the face of your business. It shapes the first impression, grabs the attention of passersby, and sets the tone for your entire brand. We create more than just an image; we build an effective navigation and advertising tool that works for you 24/7.
includes: Location analysis: We consider the building’s architecture, lighting, and surroundings to ensure the sign blends harmoniously with the environment while still standing out.
Readability and contrast: We select fonts and colors to ensure your company name is instantly legible—both day and night.
Technical expertise: We prepare a layout that accounts for production requirements (materials, lighting, mounting) so the design can be executed without compromising quality.
Visualization (3D mockup): Before production begins, you will see exactly how the sign will look on your building’s facade.
signDesignCopy.shapesIntroduction: We aren't limited to standard rectangular light boxes. A sign's shape is part of its character. Depending on your brand's needs, we can design:
shapes: Custom-shaped signs (following a logo outline or object silhouette).
Dimensional letters (with halo, face, or combined lighting).
Projecting signs (double-sided, mounted perpendicular to the wall).
signDesignCopy.result: A production-ready layout and realistic visualization to help you secure approval from your landlord or local authorities.

sampleArticle.title: We're Up and Running
sampleArticle.lead: We’ve long wanted to bring together in one place everything that Plus In Plus has become: our approach, our services, and the projects through which we put ideas to the test. Now our new website is live—and it’s more than just an updated showcase. It’s a clearer story of how we help products become cohesive and ready for growth.
sampleArticle.closing: The new Plus In Plus website is now live. Welcome.

sections.title: It's Not Just About Design
paragraphs: Plus In Plus began with a desire to make ideas clear and expressive. Over time, it became clear that a visual solution alone wasn’t enough. For a product to work, you need to tie together its goals, user experience, interface, and technological foundation.

That’s why today we take a broader view of the task—from the initial questions about the product to design, design systems, and front-end development. We care not only about how a single screen looks, but also about how all parts of the product work together.

sections.title: Why We Needed a New Website
sections.subtitle: The website was meant to answer a simple question: how can Plus In Plus be useful to your team?
paragraphs: We restructured the site to immediately highlight our main areas of focus: web design and UX, design systems, and front-end development. We also highlighted our systematic approach—where a solution helps not only launch a product but also develop it further.

The visual language also became part of this narrative: clean typography, white space, and precise details create a sense of clarity rather than clutter. And snippets of interfaces and projects allow visitors to see our approach in context.

sections.title: Experience That Grows Alongside Our Products
paragraphs: An important part of our work consists of our own projects and ecosystems: Ozone and Plus For Play. They help us view a product not just through a single mockup, but through real-world scenarios, user feedback, and iterative development.
This experience shapes how we approach new challenges: first, we understand the context; then, we build a clear system of solutions; and only then do we move on to implementation.

sections.title: What's Next
paragraphs: Launching a website isn’t the end—it’s the beginning of the next phase. We’ll be adding case studies, articles on design and development, and new insights from our product practice.
If you have an idea that needs to be turned into a clear and scalable product—tell us about it. Let’s discuss the best place to start.

lumi.metaTitle: Lumi Q1 — coding AI agent | Plus In Plus
lumi.metaDescription: Lumi Q1 technology: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B, controlled tools, an isolated repository copy, and local or cloud runtimes.
lumi.name: Lumi Q1
lumi.title: Code, tools, and boundaries in one clear system
lumi.intro: Lumi Q1 is built on Qwen2.5-Coder 7B and Ollama. The architecture separates model output from actions on a project: the model proposes a solution, while fixed code controls files, search, patches, and tests.
lumi.status: This page describes the Lumina architecture. The working integration with this website is being prepared; there is no code execution form here.
lumi.visualLabel: Animated illustration of Lumi tool calls: a task reaches the agent, tools return results, and an answer is written.

benefits.title: Access has explicit levels
benefits.description: The off, read, and permitted all modes separate reading from actions. File writes and commands require human confirmation.

benefits.title: Changes stay isolated
benefits.description: Work happens in a separate repository copy and a lumi/… branch. The main branch is never changed automatically.

benefits.title: Commands are not chosen freely
benefits.description: Fixed tools handle files, search, patches, and tests. Commands are governed by an allowlist and an audit log.

benefits.title: The model runtime is visible
benefits.description: Local, VPS, and cloud modes remain distinguishable. The active provider and any fallback are shown to the user.

sections.title: Tools instead of unrestricted access
sections.description: Lumi does not receive arbitrary control over a computer. The access level determines the available tools, and code—not a promise in a prompt—controls execution.
points: The off mode disables tools, read leaves reading and search, and all enables writes and commands under defined rules.
Changing a file or running a command requires explicit confirmation; silence means refusal.
The local CLI supports lumi undo through its change journal; the web version cannot see the developer’s disk.
sections.visualLabel: Lumi boundary diagram: files and search on the left, access policy in the centre, writes and commands behind human approval on the right.

sections.title: A separate repository copy
sections.description: The project workflow uses a temporary copy and a lumi/… branch. The main branch is not used for writes, and the decision to publish remains with a person.
points: Paths that look like secrets are filtered before a commit and surfaced in the skipped list.
Only the separate branch can be published, without force-push or an automatic pull request.
The copy is removed after publishing, rollback, or TTL expiry; the token is not stored in Git configuration.
sections.visualLabel: Lumi repository sandbox diagram: the main branch stays above, work follows a separate branch, a person chooses publishing or rollback, and the copy is cleaned up.

sections.title: Local, VPS, or cloud runtime
sections.description: Lumi’s primary runtime is local Ollama with a model based on Qwen2.5-Coder 7B. A fallback chain can improve availability, but the active endpoint and the reason for switching must remain visible.
points: Local mode keeps materials within the operator’s environment; cloud mode sends the request to an external provider.
The fallback order is local Ollama → VPS → a compatible cloud API.
Web and CLI are separate entry points: the local process works with your folder, while the server only accesses its permitted environment.
sections.visualLabel: Lumi runtime diagram: local Ollama, VPS, and cloud API are distinct routes with a visible active status.

lumi.closingDescription: Code-level boundaries reduce risk, but they do not turn a proposed patch into a production-ready solution.
closingPoints: The model can miss the project architecture or propose code that does not compile.
Tests run only from the permitted command set; their results still need to be read and understood.
Keys, passwords, and protected files must not enter the working context.
lumi.cautionTitle: What is described—and what is not connected yet
lumi.cautionText: The Lumina documents describe the agent and its CLI/web environments. On this website, the page is a technology presentation, not a working terminal or repository sandbox.

kairo.metaTitle: Kairo — AI assistant for Russian law | Plus In Plus
kairo.metaDescription: Kairo technology: LangGraph, BM25 RAG with sources, deterministic calculations, citation checks, and a two-layer answer.
kairo.name: Kairo
kairo.title: Legal information shaped into a clear next step
kairo.intro: Kairo is an informational assistant focused on Russian law. A LangGraph workflow separates facts, legal research, calculations, contract review, and answer preparation so the model does not replace verifiable tools.
kairo.status: This page describes the Lumina architecture. The working integration with this website is being prepared; there is no legal consultation form here.
kairo.visualLabel: Animated illustration of Kairo RAG: a question enters a document field, the closest sources are highlighted, and an answer is assembled with citation marks.
kairo.benefitsTitle: What makes an answer more useful

benefits.title: Research is grounded in sources
benefits.description: BM25 matches everyday wording to knowledge cards and returns references, excerpts, and links for verification.

benefits.title: Code calculates the numbers
benefits.description: Separate functions calculate duties, interest, penalties, and deadlines with a formula, legal basis, and warnings.

benefits.title: Citations and amounts are checked
benefits.description: Verification compares norms with the knowledge base and looks for amounts without a calculation or source data. Risks receive an explicit status.

benefits.title: The next step stays visible
benefits.description: A short practical answer is separate from norms, risks, and calculations. Detail remains available without obscuring what to do next.

sections.title: LangGraph controls the order of work
sections.description: A request becomes a state containing facts, a plan, and artefacts. The planner selects the required nodes, while code normalises the order: research and calculations are prepared before assessment and document drafting.
points: The state can be serialised into a SQLite checkpoint; the workflow is more than one long prompt.
Research, calculator, contract review, and drafting are separate stages, not a single opaque model response.
Document drafting can include a human-in-the-loop pause before the final response.
sections.visualLabel: Kairo graph diagram: facts and planning lead to research, calculation, and verification before the answer is formed.

sections.title: Research, calculations, and citations are checked separately
sections.description: BM25 searches knowledge cards using tokens, Russian stems, and synonyms. Calculators and citation checks are invoked by code: the model is not expected to remember a formula or invent an amount.
points: A source includes a title, reference, excerpt, score, and URL when the card provides one.
A calculation returns a formula, legal basis, and warnings; it is the authoritative source of numbers.
Verification distinguishes ok, warn, and block; the verdict exposes risk, but a lawyer makes the decision.
sections.visualLabel: Kairo verification diagram: sources pass through the model and deterministic code, with separate checks for citations, amounts, and formulas.

sections.title: A short answer and a detailed analysis
sections.description: Two layers are assembled from verified artefacts: first a practical conclusion and three to five actions, then norms, risks, calculations, sources, and quality control.
points: The short layer contains deadlines and money, required evidence, and no more than two clarifying questions.
An overly long answer is replaced by a deterministic assembly, so detail cannot hide the next step.
Documents remain drafts; when HITL is enabled, release requires a lawyer’s approval.
sections.visualLabel: Kairo two-layer answer diagram: detailed norms, risks, and calculations on the left become a short conclusion, actions, and a separate detailed analysis on the right.

kairo.closingTitle: A local environment for sensitive materials
kairo.closingDescription: Kairo can run on local Qwen2.5-14B or through a configured cloud provider. For real case materials, the architecture provides a local model and disables external transfer through server configuration.
closingPoints: The active model and mode must be visible in the interface; a cloud answer is never presented as local.
The knowledge base and versions of legal norms have a date; completeness and currency are not guaranteed.
Long documents can be truncated, and citations and practice still require professional verification.
kairo.cautionText: Responses are informational and do not replace a lawyer or individual legal advice. Current law and the circumstances of each case must be checked separately.
